quiz_questions.explanation: めったに = rarely/seldom (frequency — it snows very infrequently). なかなか = not easily (implies difficulty or resistance to happening despite expectation — awkward for weather patterns). めったに is specifically for frequency.

quiz_questions.question: 毎日走っているのに、体重が___減らない。
quiz_questions.english: Despite running every day, my weight just won't go down easily.
quiz_questions.explanation: なかなか = not easily (despite effort — the speaker is running daily but the expected result isn't coming). This is the difficulty/resistance nuance. めったに = rarely (frequency — would mean weight rarely decreases, not 'despite effort').

quiz_questions.question: このレストランは予約が___取れない。いつも満席だ。
quiz_questions.english: It's not easy to get a reservation at this restaurant. It's always full.
quiz_questions.explanation: なかなか取れない = can't easily get (despite trying — the restaurant is always full, making reservations difficult to obtain). めったに = rarely (the restaurant would rarely be able to take reservations — subtly different meaning and less natural here).

records.plain_form: その上/しかも/おまけに
records.meaning: furthermore; moreover; on top of that; what's more (additive, often emphatic or surprising)
records.detailed_explanation: Three additive conjunctions for adding emphatic information: (1) その上 = furthermore / on top of that (neutral addition, can be positive or negative). (2) しかも = moreover / what's more (adds something surprising, impressive, or emphatic). (3) おまけに = on top of that / to make matters worse/better (casual — often used when the added element makes the situation even more extreme, positive or negative). All three are used to stack additional points.
records.conjugation_rules: All three are sentence-initial or clause-initial conjunctions. They do not conjugate. [Statement 1]. その上/しかも/おまけに、[Statement 2]. Statement 2 adds to or compounds Statement 1.

usage_examples.japanese: 彼女は頭がいい。その上、親切だ。
usage_examples.reading: かのじょはあたまがいい。そのうえ、しんせつだ。
usage_examples.meaning: She's smart. On top of that, she's kind.
usage_examples.nuance: Neutral addition of another positive quality — straightforward stacking.
usage_examples.context: Describing someone's good qualities.
usage_examples.alternative: しかも親切だ (also kind — similar, with slightly more emphasis)

usage_examples.japanese: 遅刻した。おまけに、財布も忘れた。
usage_examples.reading: ちこくした。おまけに、さいふもわすれた。
usage_examples.meaning: I was late. On top of that, I also forgot my wallet.
usage_examples.nuance: おまけに adds an extra misfortune — making an already bad situation worse.
usage_examples.context: Describing a series of unfortunate events.
usage_examples.alternative: その上財布も忘れた (also more neutral tone — その上 is less 'piling on')

records.nuance_notes: Register and nuance: その上 = neutral/formal addition. しかも = emphatic/surprising addition (often impressive or unexpected). おまけに = casual, often used when the addition compounds the situation (either positively or — more commonly — negatively, as in 'to make matters worse'). Note: this week's W6D6 overlaps with W5D6's それに/しかも/その上 — the book reviews them together to emphasize register differences.

related_patterns.key_difference: それに = neutral addition (also); しかも = emphatic addition (what's more — surprising); おまけに = casual/extreme addition (to top it off)
だけでなく = not only X but also Y (contrastive addition); その上/しかも/おまけに = furthermore (cumulative, same direction)

records.common_mistakes: Using おまけに in formal writing (it's casual). Using しかも for routine, unsurprising additions (save it for emphatic/impressive extras). Treating all three as fully interchangeable — the register and emotional weight differ.

quiz_questions.question: 今日は仕事でミスをした。___、電車に乗り遅れた。最悪な日だ。
quiz_questions.english: Today I made a mistake at work. On top of that, I missed the train. What a terrible day.
quiz_questions.explanation: おまけに = on top of that (casual, compounds misfortune — 'to make matters worse'). しかも would also work but is slightly more neutral/emphatic. おまけに best captures 'and then there's this additional bad thing on top.'

quiz_questions.question: あのホテルは景色がいい。___、値段が安い。信じられない。
quiz_questions.english: That hotel has great views. Moreover, the price is cheap. Unbelievable.
quiz_questions.explanation: しかも = moreover (emphatic, surprising addition — great views AND cheap? That's impressively unexpected). おまけに is more casual. その上 is neutral. しかも best captures the 'surprisingly, also...' nuance when the addition is impressive.

quiz_questions.question: Which additive conjunction is MOST APPROPRIATE for formal written Japanese?
quiz_questions.english: Choose the connector that fits best in a formal report or essay.
quiz_questions.explanation: その上 = furthermore (neutral/formal — appropriate for academic papers, business reports, formal essays). おまけに is casual. しかも is neutral but has a spoken feel. それに is conversational. その上 is the most formal of the four.
